headline: President Clinton created an emergency board to look into labor disputes between certain railroads and unions representing their workers.
what_it_does: This order set up a Presidential Emergency Board to investigate disputes between railroads represented by the National Railway Labor Conference and their employees' unions. Under federal railway labor law, such boards usually study the dispute and recommend a settlement. Setting up a board also typically delays strikes or lockouts for a set period while it does its work. No summary was provided, so details beyond the title are limited.

who_it_affects.group: Railroad workers represented by the unions involved
who_it_affects.how: Their labor dispute was sent to a federal board for investigation, which usually puts any strike on hold for a period of time.

who_it_affects.group: Railroads represented by the National Railway Labor Conference
who_it_affects.how: Their dispute with worker unions was placed under review by a federal board, which usually also delays lockouts or changes to working conditions.
